source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year PUMS person files 2019 and 2021-2024 (2020 experimental weights excluded), people married at some point in the 12 months before the interview
target: Probability of reporting a divorce in the past 12 months (MARHD), among people married at some point in those months: a CROSS-SECTIONAL one-year incidence from one interview, not a prospective forecast
population: U.S. household and group-quarters population aged 15+, both sexes, any marriage order, married at some point in the past 12 months; the person’s own report. Same-sex and opposite-sex marriages alike
weights: ACS person weight PWGTP, normalised to mean 1 within each survey year
timing: Everything is measured at the interview, AFTER any divorce. Income, employment and occupation (the "_post" models) can be consequences of the divorce; education and state of residence can change after it too. Do not read these models as forecasts for an intact marriage.

training.note: train is a random sample of rows from the 90% of households not held out

inputs.age: age in years at the interview
inputs.marriage_years: years since the most recent wedding (survey year minus year last married)
inputs.education: Less than high school, High school or GED, Some college, Associate, Bachelor, Graduate or professional (at the interview)
inputs.state: two-letter state code of residence at the interview (50 states and DC)
inputs.income_percentile: "_post" models only: personal income percentile within the survey year among the population (0-100)
inputs.employment: "_post" models only: Employed, Unemployed, Not in labor force (at the interview)
inputs.occupation_group: "_post" models only: broad 2018 Census occupation group of the current or most recent job

abstain: forecasts for a specific future year: this is cross-sectional incidence

post_event_gain_over_background.note: logistic_additive_post vs logistic_additive on the same held-out people

population_reference.method: Weighted percentiles (p1..p99) of the held-out predicted probability of a divorce within one year (horizon 1), among test-set people (10% of households, pooled 2019 and 2021-2024); subgroups with fewer than 200 people omitted. Cross-sectional: inputs are measured at the interview.

models.label: Additive logistic (splines in age and marriage length), background inputs
Poisson gradient boosting (200 trees, depth 4), background inputs
Additive logistic + income percentile, employment, occupation (measured after the event)
Poisson gradient boosting + income, employment, occupation (measured after the event)
